words.enDefinition: a container holding supplies for immediate basic assistance

examples.en: The receptionist pointed out a first aid kit behind the library information desk.
examples.zh: 图书馆咨询台的工作人员指了指柜台后面的「急救包」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the first aid kit traveled with us on field trips.
examples.zh: 导师问我们外出考察时会不会随身带上「急救包」。

words.enDefinition: a designated place offering basic help at a venue

examples.en: The map showed a first aid station next to the festival's volunteer tent.
examples.zh: 地图上标明节日志愿者帐篷旁有一个「现场急救点」。

examples.en: I asked the event steward where to find the first aid station.
examples.zh: 我问活动现场的引导员到哪里能找到「现场急救点」。

words.enDefinition: a room set aside for basic assistance on site

examples.en: The sports centre's first aid room was beside the accessible changing rooms.
examples.zh: 体育中心的「急救室」就在无障碍更衣室旁边。

examples.en: The sign for the first aid room was partly hidden by the open door.
examples.zh: 「急救室」的标牌被敞开的门挡住了一部分。

collocations: directions to the first aid room
a sign for the first aid room

words.enDefinition: a person trained and designated to give basic first aid at a venue or workplace

examples.en: The receptionist radioed a first aider after a visitor fell in the foyer.
examples.zh: 一位访客在门厅摔倒后，接待员用对讲机联系了「受训急救员」。

examples.en: A first aider spoke with the student near the end of the match.
examples.zh: 比赛快结束时，一名「受训急救员」和那位学生交谈了几句。

words.enDefinition: a medical responder assigned to an organized event

examples.en: An event medic was already talking to the runner when I reached the tent.
examples.zh: 我赶到帐篷时，一名「活动现场医护人员」已经在和那位跑步者说话了。

examples.en: One event medic wore a bright vest with the festival logo on it.
examples.zh: 一名「活动现场医护人员」穿着印有节日标志的亮色背心。

words.enDefinition: a staff member who responds to campus safety concerns

examples.en: A campus safety officer met us outside the gym after the incident.
examples.zh: 事发后，一名「校园安全员」在体育馆外和我们会合。

examples.en: I told the campus safety officer that I had only heard the fall.
examples.zh: 我告诉「校园安全员」，我只听见了摔倒时的响声。

collocations: report something to a campus safety officer
the campus safety officer on duty

words.enDefinition: arrangements for trained help to be available during an event

examples.en: Our club president asked about first aid cover for the open day.
examples.zh: 社团负责人询问了开放日的「现场急救保障」安排。

examples.en: The organiser confirmed that there would be first aid cover throughout the tournament.
examples.zh: 组织者确认比赛全程都会有「现场急救保障」。

collocations: first aid cover for an event

words.enDefinition: a sign identifying where basic assistance or equipment is available

examples.en: A green first aid sign was visible at the end of the corridor.
examples.zh: 走廊尽头可以看到一个绿色的「急救标志」。

examples.en: I spotted the first aid sign above a door behind the reception desk.
examples.zh: 我看见接待台后面的一扇门上方有「急救标志」。

words.enDefinition: a portable device that analyses heart rhythm and can deliver a shock

examples.en: The sports hall has an automated external defibrillator in a clearly marked cabinet.
examples.zh: 体育馆有一台「自动体外除颤器」，放在有清楚标识的柜子里。

examples.en: Our campus tour guide showed us where the automated external defibrillator was kept.
examples.zh: 校园参观时，向导给我们指了「自动体外除颤器」放在哪里。

collocations: a publicly accessible automated external defibrillator

words.enDefinition: a marked case that houses an emergency defibrillator

examples.en: I saw the defibrillator cabinet beside the lift on my way to class.
examples.zh: 我去上课时看见电梯旁有个「除颤器存放柜」。

examples.en: A volunteer reported that the label on the defibrillator cabinet was hard to read.
examples.zh: 一名志愿者反映，「除颤器存放柜」上的标签不好辨认。

words.enDefinition: a marker showing where a defibrillator is located

examples.en: The defibrillator sign was high enough to see even from the back row.
examples.zh: 「除颤器标识」挂得很高，坐在最后一排也能看见。

examples.en: I saw a defibrillator sign above the noticeboard near the corridor entrance.
examples.zh: 我看见走廊入口旁的公告板上方有个「除颤器标识」。

words.enDefinition: an adhesive contact that connects a device electrically to skin

examples.en: The drawing on the packet showed the outline of an electrode pad.
examples.zh: 包装袋上的图画出了「电极贴片」的轮廓。

examples.en: The instructor held up a sealed electrode pad during our equipment tour.
examples.zh: 介绍设备时，讲解员举起了一片还没拆封的「电极贴片」。

words.enDefinition: a lightweight cover designed to reduce body heat loss

examples.en: The foil emergency blanket was still folded inside its small silver packet.
examples.zh: 那张铝膜「应急保温毯」还折叠着装在小小的银色袋子里。

examples.en: The equipment checklist included an emergency blanket for the outdoor team event.
examples.zh: 户外团队活动的装备清单上列了一张「应急保温毯」。

words.enDefinition: single-use hand coverings that provide a protective barrier

examples.en: The new first aid supplies included a carton of disposable gloves for volunteers.
examples.zh: 新到的急救用品里有一盒供志愿者用的「一次性手套」。

examples.en: I counted the unopened packs of disposable gloves listed on the inventory sheet.
examples.zh: 我按库存表数了还没拆封的「一次性手套」有几包。

words.enDefinition: a small square of woven fabric used as a dressing

examples.en: The sealed gauze pad was tucked into the side pocket of the kit.
examples.zh: 没拆封的「纱布垫」塞在急救包的侧袋里。

examples.en: I could read the words gauze pad through the clear lid of the box.
examples.zh: 透过透明盒盖，我能看见包装上写的「纱布垫」。

words.enDefinition: a small wound cover with self-sticking edges

examples.en: I spotted a wrapped adhesive bandage in the kit by the reception desk.
examples.zh: 我看见接待台旁的急救包里有一片没拆封的「创可贴」。

examples.en: A student volunteer asked whether there was an adhesive bandage in the drawer.
examples.zh: 一名学生志愿者问抽屉里还有没有「创可贴」。

words.enDefinition: a protective covering made to sit over a wound

examples.en: The wound dressing was listed separately from the rolls of white medical tape.
examples.zh: 清单上「伤口敷料」和一卷卷白色医用胶带是分开列出的。

examples.en: The label showed that the wound dressing was in a sealed packet.
examples.zh: 标签注明这片「伤口敷料」装在密封袋里。

collocations: a packet containing a wound dressing

words.enDefinition: adhesive tape made for securing dressings or medical materials

examples.en: A roll of medical tape was inside the clear pocket on the left.
examples.zh: 左边的透明袋里放着一卷「医用胶带」。

examples.en: I read the label on the medical tape while sorting the new supplies.
examples.zh: 整理新到的用品时，我看了「医用胶带」上的标签。

words.enDefinition: a large triangular piece of cloth included in first aid supplies

examples.en: A diagram of the triangular bandage appeared on the outside of its wrapper.
examples.zh: 包装外面印了「三角绷带」的示意图。

examples.en: The equipment list included a triangular bandage in its own sealed pouch.
examples.zh: 装备清单上有一条单独用袋子密封的「三角绷带」。

words.enDefinition: a stretchable strip of fabric used as a wrap

examples.en: The elastic bandage was on the shelf with the other unopened wraps.
examples.zh: 那卷「弹力绷带」和其他未拆封的绷带放在同一个架子上。

examples.en: I wrote the width of the elastic bandage beside its name on the inventory.
examples.zh: 我在库存表上的「弹力绷带」旁记了它的宽度。

words.enDefinition: a sealed pouch that becomes cold without prior refrigeration

examples.en: The coach read the label on the instant cold pack from the kit.
examples.zh: 教练看了急救包里「速冷袋」上的标签。

examples.en: The inventory showed one instant cold pack in each of the portable bags.
examples.zh: 库存表上写着每个便携急救包里都放有一个「速冷袋」。

collocations: a box of instant cold packs

words.enDefinition: materials kept on hand for basic immediate help

examples.en: The evening custodian showed me where the first aid supplies were stored.
examples.zh: 晚班管理员告诉我「急救用品」存放在哪里。

examples.en: Our department keeps extra first aid supplies in a locked cupboard downstairs.
examples.zh: 我们系在楼下上锁的柜子里备了额外的「急救用品」。

collocations: a checklist of first aid supplies
a cupboard for first aid supplies

words.enDefinition: a face barrier designed for giving rescue breaths

examples.en: The volunteer recognised the resuscitation mask from a diagram in the training booklet.
examples.zh: 志愿者凭培训手册上的示意图认出了「复苏面罩」。

examples.en: The resuscitation mask was stored in a blue case with an illustrated label.
examples.zh: 「复苏面罩」放在蓝色盒子里，盒上贴着有图示的标签。

collocations: a case for a resuscitation mask

words.enDefinition: a fixed facility for rinsing material from the eyes

examples.en: The lab tour included the eyewash station near the double doors by the entrance.
examples.zh: 实验室参观时介绍了入口对开门旁的「紧急洗眼装置」。

examples.en: The technician checked that the eyewash station was marked on the new floor plan.
examples.zh: 技术员核对了新平面图上是否标出了「紧急洗眼装置」。

collocations: a sign for the eyewash station

words.enDefinition: a workplace fixture designed to rinse accidental contamination from the body

examples.en: The safety shower was marked on the map outside the chemistry lab.
examples.zh: 化学实验室门外的图上标有「应急冲淋装置」。

examples.en: Our guide pointed out the yellow sign above the safety shower near reception.
examples.zh: 向导给我们指了接待处附近「应急冲淋装置」上方的黄色标牌。

collocations: the location of a safety shower

words.enDefinition: a wristband displaying important health information for responders

examples.en: The student pointed out her medical alert bracelet when she spoke to the officer.
examples.zh: 那名学生和安全员说话时，指给对方看了自己的「医疗警示手链」。

examples.en: The roommate told staff that the medical alert bracelet had an emergency number engraved on it.
examples.zh: 室友告诉工作人员，「医疗警示手链」上刻着紧急联系号码。

collocations: information on a medical alert bracelet

words.enDefinition: a portable card listing important health information for responders

examples.en: The student said her medical alert card was in the front of her wallet.
examples.zh: 那名学生说，她的「医疗警示卡」放在钱包最前面的夹层里。

examples.en: The volunteer noticed the medical alert card had emergency details printed on both sides.
examples.zh: 志愿者注意到，「医疗警示卡」两面都印了紧急情况所需的信息。

collocations: details on a medical alert card

words.enDefinition: blunt-tipped scissors designed to cut sturdy material in emergencies

examples.en: The instructor showed a sealed pair of trauma shears during the equipment orientation.
examples.zh: 介绍设备时，讲解员展示了一把没拆封的「急救剪」。

examples.en: I found the trauma shears in the compartment with the bright orange zipper.
examples.zh: 我在有亮橙色拉链的夹层里找到了「急救剪」。

words.enDefinition: a single-use protective covering worn over the front of clothing

examples.en: The volunteer checking supplies found a disposable apron at the bottom of the box.
examples.zh: 清点用品的志愿者在箱底找到了一条「一次性围裙」。

examples.en: Each disposable apron came in its own wrapper with a printed inventory code.
examples.zh: 每条「一次性围裙」都有独立包装，印着库存编号。

words.enDefinition: a shaped dressing designed to cover an eye

examples.en: The eye pad was in a separate sleeve at the top of the kit.
examples.zh: 「眼部敷垫」单独装在急救包上方的一个套袋里。

examples.en: I asked whether the sealed eye pad belonged with the other dressings.
examples.zh: 我问这片没拆封的「眼部敷垫」是否应该和其他敷料放在一起。

words.enDefinition: to fall unexpectedly, especially while moving or playing a sport

examples.en: I saw him take a fall near the end of basketball practice.
examples.zh: 篮球训练快结束时，我看见他「摔了一跤」。

examples.en: She said she might take a fall if the loose board moved again.
examples.zh: 她说，那块松动的板子要是再挪动，她可能会「摔一跤」。

collocations: take a fall on the stairs
take a fall on the court

words.enDefinition: to lose your footing on a surface and fall

examples.en: I saw someone slip and fall as they came through the gym doors.
examples.zh: 我看见有人刚进体育馆大门就「滑倒了」。

examples.en: They were worried a visitor might slip and fall near the leaking water fountain.
examples.zh: 他们担心有访客会在漏水的饮水机旁「滑倒」。

collocations: slip and fall on a wet floor

words.enDefinition: to hit a surface with a body part after falling

examples.en: I saw him land on his left side at the bottom of the steps.
examples.zh: 我看见他摔到台阶底下时，「左侧身体先着地」。

examples.en: She told the coach she had tried not to land on her wrist.
examples.zh: 她告诉教练，自己摔倒时尽量没让「手腕先着地」。

words.enDefinition: to strike your head against something, often during a fall

examples.en: Did you hit your head on the doorframe or just your shoulder?
examples.zh: 你是「撞到了头」，还是只有肩膀撞上了门框？

examples.en: If you did hit your head, was it on the table or the floor?
examples.zh: 如果你确实「撞到了头」，是撞在桌子上还是地上？

collocations: hit your head on the floor
hit your head on a doorframe
hit your head during a fall

words.enDefinition: physical harm to the head caused by an impact or accident

examples.en: I told the supervisor I was unsure whether there was a head injury.
examples.zh: 我告诉主管，我不确定他是否「头部伤情」。

examples.en: I wasn't close enough to tell whether he had a head injury.
examples.zh: 我离得不够近，看不清他「头部有没有受伤」。

collocations: a head injury after a fall

words.enDefinition: to drop unexpectedly from a place above ground level

examples.en: The tutor asked whether she had seen anyone fall from a height outside.
examples.zh: 导师问她有没有看见外面有人「从高处坠落」。

examples.en: You couldn't see anyone fall from a height from where we were standing.
examples.zh: 从我们站的位置看不到有人「从高处坠落」。

collocations: fall from a height at work
fall from a height onto concrete
see someone fall from a height

words.enDefinition: to injure a muscle by overstretching it or exerting it suddenly

examples.en: I thought I might pull a muscle when the heavy box shifted suddenly.
examples.zh: 那个重箱子突然移位时，我以为自己可能会「拉伤肌肉」。

examples.en: My teammate said she could pull a muscle if she kept sprinting that hard.
examples.zh: 队友说，如果她继续这么拼命地冲刺，可能会「拉伤肌肉」。

collocations: pull a muscle in your back

words.enDefinition: to twist your ankle sideways unexpectedly, often while stepping or landing

examples.en: Did you roll your ankle when you stepped off the edge of the path?
examples.zh: 你从小路边缘迈下去时「崴脚了」吗？

examples.en: It's easy to roll your ankle on the uneven grass behind the gym.
examples.zh: 体育馆后面那片草地不平，很容易「崴脚」。

collocations: roll your ankle on uneven ground
roll your ankle when you land

words.enDefinition: to injure a finger by forcing its tip back suddenly

examples.en: Did you jam your finger when you tried to catch that pass?
examples.zh: 你试着接那个传球时「戳伤手指」了吗？

examples.en: I told the new player it was easy to jam your finger catching that ball.
examples.zh: 我告诉新队员，接那个球很容易「戳伤手指」。

collocations: jam your finger catching a ball
jam your finger against the wall

words.enDefinition: to have a finger trapped as something closes or moves

examples.en: Did you catch your finger in the folding chair when it closed?
examples.zh: 折叠椅合上时，你「把手指夹在里面了」吗？

examples.en: It's easy to catch your finger in that drawer when it shuts quickly.
examples.zh: 那个抽屉合得快时，很容易「把手指夹在里面」。

collocations: catch your finger in a door
catch your finger in a drawer
catch your finger in a hinge

words.enDefinition: to have dust, grit or another object enter an eye

examples.en: Did you get something in your eye when the wind picked up?
examples.zh: 刚才刮起风的时候，你「眼里进了东西」吗？

examples.en: It's easy to get something in your eye when the practice field gets dusty.
examples.zh: 训练场上尘土飞起来时，很容易「眼里进东西」。

collocations: get something in your eye outdoors
get something in your eye while cycling
think you might get something in your eye

words.enDefinition: to rub skin off the knee against a rough surface

examples.en: Did you scrape your knee on the gravel when you fell outside?
examples.zh: 你刚才在外面摔倒时，「膝盖被碎石擦伤了」吗？

examples.en: How did you scrape your knee if you landed on your hands?
examples.zh: 如果是手先着地，你是怎么「擦伤膝盖」的？

collocations: scrape your knee in a fall

words.enDefinition: to have a tiny sharp piece, often wood, pierce the skin

examples.en: Did you get a splinter while moving the old benches after practice?
examples.zh: 训练后搬旧长凳的时候，你「被木刺扎到了」吗？

examples.en: You can get a splinter from the unfinished wood on that workshop table.
examples.zh: 那张工坊工作台的木料没打磨，容易让人「被木刺扎到」。

collocations: get a splinter in your palm
get a splinter from a bench
get a splinter in your thumb

words.enDefinition: a small skin cut made by the edge of paper

examples.en: I noticed a paper cut after sorting the handouts for our afternoon seminar.
examples.zh: 我给下午的研讨课整理讲义后，发现手上有道「纸划伤」。

examples.en: The volunteer said the mark was a paper cut from opening the envelope.
examples.zh: 那名志愿者说，那道小口子是拆信封时「被纸划伤」留下的。

collocations: a paper cut on your thumb

words.enDefinition: an opening in the skin extending into deeper tissue

examples.en: The pottery teacher noticed a deep cut when I showed her my finger.
examples.zh: 我把手指给陶艺老师看时，她发现了一道「较深的割伤」。

examples.en: My roommate said the mark looked like a deep cut under the bright light.
examples.zh: 室友说，在亮灯下，那道伤痕看起来像「较深的割伤」。

collocations: a deep cut on the hand
a deep cut from broken glass

words.enDefinition: a narrow wound made by something pointed piercing the skin

examples.en: I saw what looked like a small puncture wound after she stepped on a tack.
examples.zh: 她踩到图钉后，我看到一处像是「小小的刺伤伤口」。

examples.en: The student described a puncture wound on his hand where the wire had caught him.
examples.zh: 那名学生描述了手被金属丝挂到后留下的「刺伤伤口」。

collocations: a puncture wound in the foot

words.enDefinition: to accidentally injure your skin against a sharp object

examples.en: Did you cut yourself on a piece of broken glass near the door?
examples.zh: 你是「被门边的一块碎玻璃割伤」的吗？

examples.en: You could cut yourself on that chipped mug if you grab the rim there.
examples.zh: 要是捏住那个破杯子的杯口，你可能会「被它割伤」。

collocations: cut yourself on a sharp edge

words.enDefinition: a shallow area of skin scraped by a rough surface

examples.en: I showed the coach the graze on my elbow after the match.
examples.zh: 比赛结束后，我把胳膊肘上的「皮肤擦伤」给教练看了。

examples.en: The student said the mark above her sock was just an old graze.
examples.zh: 那名学生说，袜子上沿那道印子只是以前的「皮肤擦伤」。

words.enDefinition: a cut in the lip caused by an impact

examples.en: I noticed a split lip when my teammate turned toward the bench.
examples.zh: 队友转身朝替补席走来时，我看到他「嘴唇裂伤了」。

examples.en: A split lip was the only injury she mentioned after colliding with another player.
examples.zh: 和另一名队员撞上后，她只说自己「嘴唇裂伤」。

collocations: a split lip after a collision

words.enDefinition: to make contact with the ground after falling

examples.en: I heard his shoulder hit the ground before I saw him lying there.
examples.zh: 我先听到他的肩膀「撞到地面」的声音，接着才看到他躺在那里。

examples.en: She saw his left elbow hit the ground as he fell sideways.
examples.zh: 她看见他往旁边倒下时，左肘「撞到了地面」。

words.enDefinition: to have one foot snagged on an object while moving

examples.en: It's easy to catch a foot on that cable under the table.
examples.zh: 桌子底下那根线很容易「绊住脚」。

examples.en: I saw him catch a foot on the leg of a folding chair.
examples.zh: 我看见他「被一把折叠椅的椅腿绊住了脚」。

collocations: catch a foot on a cable
catch a foot on a step
catch a foot on the corner of a mat

words.enDefinition: to stop having a secure hold on the ground with your feet

examples.en: Did you lose your footing halfway down the stairs outside the hall?
examples.zh: 你是走到礼堂外的台阶中段时「脚下没站稳」的吗？

examples.en: It's easy to lose your footing where the loose gravel meets the pavement.
examples.zh: 松散碎石和硬路面交接的地方，很容易「脚下没站稳」。

collocations: lose your footing on loose gravel
lose your footing on the stairs

words.enDefinition: the rear part of the head above the neck

examples.en: My classmate said the back of the head hit the wall first.
examples.zh: 我同学说，那个人先是「后脑勺」撞到了墙。

examples.en: The student pointed to the back of the head when describing the impact.
examples.zh: 描述撞击时，那名学生指了指自己的「后脑勺」。

collocations: the back of the head struck the floor
a bump to the back of the head
point to the back of the head

words.enDefinition: the inner surface of the hand between wrist and fingers

examples.en: The small cut was on the palm of the hand, near the thumb.
examples.zh: 那道小口子在「手掌」上，靠近拇指。

examples.en: She pointed to the palm of the hand while talking to the first aider.
examples.zh: 她和急救员交谈时，指了指自己的「手掌」。

collocations: a cut on the palm of the hand
the centre of the palm of the hand
a mark on the palm of the hand

words.enDefinition: the joints of the fingers, especially where they meet the hand

examples.en: I saw marks across his knuckles after he caught his hand in the door.
examples.zh: 他的手被门夹到后，我看到他的「手指关节」上有几道印子。

examples.en: She showed the first aider which knuckles had knocked against the table.
examples.zh: 她给急救员看了是哪几个「手指关节」撞到了桌子。

words.enDefinition: the part of the leg between the knee and ankle

examples.en: The player pointed to her lower leg when asked where she had landed.
examples.zh: 有人问她是哪里先着地时，那名队员指了指自己的「小腿」。

examples.en: His lower leg had caught on the metal edge of the bench.
examples.zh: 他的「小腿」刚才卡在长凳的金属边上了。

collocations: the front of the lower leg
a mark on the lower leg

words.enDefinition: the part of the arm between the shoulder and elbow

examples.en: I saw her upper arm strike the doorframe as she turned to leave.
examples.zh: 她转身要离开时，我看见她的「上臂」撞到了门框。

examples.en: He said the mark on his upper arm was from last week's practice.
examples.zh: 他说「上臂」上的那道印子是上周训练时留下的。

collocations: the inside of the upper arm
a bruise on the upper arm
the upper arm near the shoulder

words.enDefinition: a lip noticeably larger than usual due to swelling

examples.en: I could see a swollen lip when she turned toward the light.
examples.zh: 她转向有光的地方时，我看见她的「嘴唇肿了」。

examples.en: The instructor asked whether the swollen lip had already been there before practice.
examples.zh: 教练问她训练前是不是就已经「嘴唇肿了」。

collocations: a swollen lip after a collision

words.enDefinition: a visible mark left on the skin by a burn

examples.en: The student showed the lab supervisor a small burn mark on his forearm.
examples.zh: 那名学生给实验室主管看了前臂上的一小块「灼伤痕迹」。

examples.en: I noticed a burn mark when she rolled up the sleeve of her jacket.
examples.zh: 她卷起上衣袖子时，我看见了一处「灼伤痕迹」。

collocations: a burn mark on the wrist

words.enDefinition: a burn caused by hot liquid or steam

examples.en: The kitchen worker reported a scald after hot water spilled across her wrist.
examples.zh: 热水洒在手腕上后，厨房工作人员报告说自己「烫伤了」。

examples.en: I heard the volunteer say the red mark was a scald from steam.
examples.zh: 我听见志愿者说那片红印是蒸汽造成的「烫伤」。

words.enDefinition: a raised area on the skin after an impact

examples.en: A small bump was visible above his eyebrow when he looked up.
examples.zh: 他抬头时，可以看到眉毛上面「撞起了一个小包」。

examples.en: She said the bump on her forehead appeared right after the fall.
examples.zh: 她说额头上的「包」是摔倒后立刻鼓起来的。

collocations: a small bump above the eyebrow
notice a bump after a fall

words.enDefinition: a fall that another person saw happen

examples.en: The campus form had a box for a witnessed fall during an event.
examples.zh: 校园表格有一栏，用来注明活动中的「摔倒有人目睹」。

examples.en: I marked it as a witnessed fall because I had seen her trip.
examples.zh: 我当时看见她绊倒了，所以标记为「有人目睹的摔倒」。

words.enDefinition: a fall that nobody saw as it happened

examples.en: The supervisor recorded an unwitnessed fall because staff arrived after the sound.
examples.zh: 工作人员听到声响后才赶到，因此主管记录为「无人目睹的摔倒」。

examples.en: I was asked whether to mark the incident as an unwitnessed fall.
examples.zh: 有人问我，这件事是不是要标成「无人目睹的摔倒」。

collocations: an unwitnessed fall in the hallway

words.enDefinition: to become unaware of your surroundings and unable to respond

examples.en: I didn't see her lose consciousness because I was facing the other way.
examples.zh: 我当时朝着另一边，没看到她「失去意识」。

examples.en: The first aider asked whether anyone had seen him lose consciousness at the gym.
examples.zh: 急救员问，有没有人在体育馆看见他「失去意识」。

words.enDefinition: to become conscious again after being unconscious

examples.en: The staff member asked whether I had seen him regain consciousness at all.
examples.zh: 那位工作人员问，我有没有看到他「恢复意识」。

examples.en: She didn't regain consciousness until after the event medic had reached the room.
examples.zh: 直到现场医护人员赶到房间后，她才「恢复意识」。

collocations: regain consciousness a few minutes later

words.enDefinition: not reacting when someone speaks to you or tries to get your attention

examples.en: He was unresponsive when the librarian first called to him from the doorway.
examples.zh: 图书管理员第一次站在门口喊他时，他「没有反应」。

examples.en: I told the safety officer she appeared unresponsive when I first saw her.
examples.zh: 我告诉安全员，我刚看见她时，她似乎「没有反应」。

words.enDefinition: leaning forward or sideways with the body hanging loosely

examples.en: I found him slumped over the desk when I arrived for the tutorial.
examples.zh: 我到教室上辅导课时，发现他「瘫靠在桌上」。

examples.en: She was slumped over the arm of the chair when we came in.
examples.zh: 我们进来时，她「瘫靠在椅子的扶手上」。

collocations: slumped over the arm of a chair

words.enDefinition: to become loose and no longer hold your body upright

examples.en: I saw him go limp just as he reached the end of the bench.
examples.zh: 我看见他到长凳尽头时「全身突然发软」。

examples.en: The instructor asked what he was doing before I saw him go limp.
examples.zh: 教练问，我看见他「全身突然发软」之前，他在做什么。

words.enDefinition: to react when someone calls you by name

examples.en: The staff member asked if you could respond to your name after you fell.
examples.zh: 工作人员问，你摔倒后能不能「听到自己名字就有反应」。

examples.en: You didn't respond to your name when I called from across the room.
examples.zh: 我隔着房间喊了你的名字，可你「没有反应」。

collocations: respond to your name right away
able to respond to your name

words.enDefinition: awake, aware and able to speak with someone

examples.en: He was alert and talking when the receptionist came over a moment later.
examples.zh: 过了一会儿，接待员走过来时，他「清醒着，还在说话」。

examples.en: I told the organiser she was alert and talking when I left the room.
examples.zh: 我告诉组织者，我离开房间时，她「清醒着，能说话」。

words.enDefinition: to appear noticeably lighter in the face than usual

examples.en: You look pale, and I noticed that you stopped talking halfway through the presentation.
examples.zh: 你「脸色看起来很苍白」，我还注意到你做报告做到一半就没再说话了。

examples.en: The student didn't look pale until he came back into the brighter room.
examples.zh: 那名学生回到光线更亮的房间后，才显得「脸色苍白」。

words.enDefinition: to soak through a covering such as a dressing or clothing

examples.en: I saw the wound bleed through his sleeve and told a member of staff.
examples.zh: 我看见血「渗透到衣袖外面」，就告诉了工作人员。

examples.en: I told the first aider I had seen the cut bleed through the bandage.
examples.zh: 我告诉急救员，我看见伤口的血「渗透到绷带外面」了。

words.enDefinition: to become larger or puffier, often after a knock or irritation

examples.en: His finger began to swell up while we waited for the coach.
examples.zh: 我们等教练时，他的手指开始「肿起来」。

examples.en: I told her the skin around my wrist had started to swell up.
examples.zh: 我告诉她，我手腕周围的皮肤开始「肿起来」了。

words.enDefinition: a leg abruptly stopped being able to support a person's weight

examples.en: She said her leg gave way as she stepped down from the platform.
examples.zh: 她说，迈下站台时，她的「腿突然一软」。

examples.en: I saw him reach for the railing when his leg gave way.
examples.zh: 他的「腿突然一软」时，我看见他伸手去扶栏杆。

collocations: her leg gave way on the stairs
his leg gave way beneath him

words.enDefinition: noticeably upset or unsettled after a frightening experience

examples.en: The student was visibly shaken when her classmate asked what had happened.
examples.zh: 同学问发生了什么时，那名学生「明显受惊」。

examples.en: He was visibly shaken after seeing the accident in the workshop.
examples.zh: 在工坊目睹事故后，他「明显受惊」。

words.enDefinition: no outward sign of an injury

examples.en: I reported no visible injury because I couldn't see a mark from where I stood.
examples.zh: 我从自己站的位置没看到伤痕，就报告说「没有看到外伤」。

examples.en: The note said no visible injury, but it also recorded her account of the fall.
examples.zh: 记录写着「没有可见外伤」，也写下了她讲述的摔倒经过。

collocations: no visible injury to the arm

words.enDefinition: not able to get upright on one's feet

examples.en: The student said she was unable to stand after her foot slipped on the steps.
examples.zh: 那名学生说，她在台阶上一脚滑倒后就「无法站立」。

examples.en: I reported that he was unable to stand when the coach asked for an update.
examples.zh: 教练问现在怎样了，我说他「无法站立」。

words.enDefinition: to rise after sitting or falling without another person's help

examples.en: Were you able to get up on your own after slipping outside the hall?
examples.zh: 你在礼堂外面滑倒后，能「自己站起来」吗？

examples.en: The coach asked if you could get up on your own after the fall.
examples.zh: 教练问，你摔倒后能不能「自己站起来」。

collocations: able to get up on your own
try to get up on your own
couldn't get up on your own

words.enDefinition: unable to lift the eyelids of one eye

examples.en: I can't open one eye since I got something in it outside.
examples.zh: 我在外面眼里进了东西，现在「一只眼睛睁不开」。

examples.en: My roommate said, “I can't open one eye,” when I asked what was wrong.
examples.zh: 我问室友怎么了，对方说「我一只眼睛睁不开」。

collocations: say you can't open one eye

words.enDefinition: a question asking someone to indicate the part that hurts

examples.en: The coach asked, “Where does it hurt?” after the player described her fall.
examples.zh: 队员说完是怎么摔倒的，教练问她「哪儿疼？」

examples.en: “Where does it hurt?” my roommate asked when I pointed to my shoulder.
examples.zh: 我指向肩膀时，室友问「哪儿疼？」

collocations: “Where does it hurt when you move?”

words.enDefinition: a question checking whether someone can hear you speak

examples.en: “Can you hear me?” the instructor asked when the student looked up.
examples.zh: 学生抬头时，老师问「你听得见我吗？」

examples.en: A volunteer crouched nearby and quietly asked, “Can you hear me?”
examples.zh: 一名志愿者在旁边蹲下，轻声问「你听得见我吗？」

words.expression: can you tell me what happened
words.lemma: can you tell me what happened
words.enDefinition: a polite request for the other person to describe what occurred
acceptedEnVariants: can you tell me what happened

examples.en: “Can you tell me what happened?” the officer asked the student by the door.
examples.zh: 安全员问门边的学生「能说说发生了什么吗？」

examples.en: The coach sat beside me and asked, “Can you tell me what happened?”
examples.zh: 教练坐到我旁边，问「能说说发生了什么吗？」

collocations: ask “Can you tell me what happened?”
“Can you tell me what happened first?”
“Can you tell me what happened next?”

words.enDefinition: a question asking whether someone recalls the events

examples.en: “Do you remember what happened?” the teacher asked when she came over.
examples.zh: 老师走过来时问「你记得发生了什么吗？」

examples.en: I had only heard a noise, so I asked, “Do you remember what happened?”
examples.zh: 我只听到一声响，于是问「你记得发生了什么吗？」

collocations: “Do you remember what happened before you fell?”

words.enDefinition: a statement clarifying that the speaker did not witness the event

examples.en: I didn't see what happened, but I heard the chair fall behind me.
examples.zh: 「我没看见事情经过」，只听见身后有把椅子倒了。

examples.en: “I didn't see what happened,” I told the officer who came to the workshop.
examples.zh: 我告诉赶到工坊的安全员「我没看见事情经过」。

collocations: “I didn't see what happened before the fall”
“I didn't see what happened, but I heard it”

words.enDefinition: a record describing an injury and the circumstances around it

examples.en: The club's injury report asked which part of the body had been hurt.
examples.zh: 社团的「受伤情况报告」要求填写受伤的身体部位。

examples.en: I added the time to the injury report after checking the rehearsal schedule.
examples.zh: 我看了排练安排表后，把时间补到了「受伤情况报告」里。

words.enDefinition: to tell a responsible person or organization about an injury

examples.en: I went to the counter to report an injury in the rehearsal room.
examples.zh: 我到柜台「报告排练室里有人受伤」。

examples.en: The instructor showed us where to report an injury on the campus website.
examples.zh: 老师给我们看了怎样在校园网站上「报告有人受伤」。

collocations: report an injury to a supervisor
report an injury at the desk

words.enDefinition: the approximate time at which an event occurred

examples.en: I remembered roughly when it happened because our class had just started.
examples.zh: 我记得事情「大概什么时候发生的」，因为当时刚开始上课。

examples.en: The officer asked roughly when it happened and whether the room was crowded.
examples.zh: 安全员问事情「大概什么时候发生的」，当时房间里人多不多。

words.enDefinition: to make a written record of an event as you recall it

examples.en: The supervisor asked me to write down what happened while I remembered it clearly.
examples.zh: 主管让我趁还记得清楚时「记下事情经过」。

examples.en: I stayed after the rehearsal to write down what happened in the hallway.
examples.zh: 排练后我留了下来，「记下走廊里发生的事」。

collocations: ask someone to write down what happened
write down what happened in order
write down what happened while it's fresh

words.enDefinition: to say how someone fell and what you observed

examples.en: The staff member asked me to describe the fall from where I stood.
examples.zh: 工作人员让我按我站的位置看到的情况「描述摔倒经过」。

examples.en: I couldn't describe the fall because I had only heard the sound.
examples.zh: 我只听到了响声，所以说不出「摔倒的经过」。

collocations: describe the fall in your own words
ask a witness to describe the fall
describe the fall as you remember it

words.enDefinition: the place where a feeling or event first began

examples.en: When I mentioned the pain, the first aider asked where it started.
examples.zh: 我提到疼痛时，急救员问我是「从哪里开始疼的」。

examples.en: I could point to where it started before I felt it in my shoulder.
examples.zh: 我能指出「最开始疼的地方」，疼痛后来延到了肩膀。

words.enDefinition: a phrase introducing what the speaker actually witnessed

examples.en: “Here's what I saw,” I said when the officer asked me to start.
examples.zh: 安全员请我开始说，我开口道「我看到的是这样的」。

examples.en: My classmate said, “Here's what I saw,” and pointed toward the folding chairs.
examples.zh: 同学指了指那几把折叠椅，说「我看到的是这样的」。

collocations: “Here's what I saw from the doorway”
“Here's what I saw before I left”

words.enDefinition: a question asking whether another part of the body is injured

examples.en: “Are you hurt anywhere else?” the first aider asked after hearing about my arm.
examples.zh: 听我说完胳膊的情况后，急救员问「还有别的地方受伤吗？」

examples.en: My teammate asked, “Are you hurt anywhere else?” when I pointed to my knee.
examples.zh: 我指了指膝盖，队友问「还有别的地方受伤吗？」

collocations: “Are you hurt anywhere else besides your arm?”
“Before we talk to staff, are you hurt anywhere else?”

words.enDefinition: to stop being able to remain upright and steady

examples.en: Did you lose your balance before your foot reached the bottom step?
examples.zh: 你的脚还没踩到最下面一级台阶时，就「失去平衡」了吗？

examples.en: Was it the moving handrail that made you lose your balance on the stairs?
examples.zh: 是扶手晃动让你在楼梯上「失去平衡」的吗？

collocations: lose your balance on the stairs

words.enDefinition: to go and bring a teacher to where help is needed

examples.en: Could you get the teacher while I tell the receptionist what happened?
examples.zh: 你能「去找老师过来」吗？我来跟接待员说发生了什么。

examples.en: I went to get the teacher from the classroom across the hall.
examples.zh: 我去了对面教室，「把老师叫过来」。

collocations: ask someone to get the teacher
get the teacher from the next room

words.enDefinition: to fetch a staff member from a reception desk

examples.en: Could you get someone from reception to come downstairs for a moment?
examples.zh: 你能「去前台找个人下楼来」一下吗？

examples.en: My classmate went to get someone from reception while I explained the situation.
examples.zh: 我在说明情况时，同学「去前台找人过来」。

collocations: go and get someone from reception
ask someone to get someone from reception
get someone from reception to come upstairs

words.enDefinition: to leave your location to find someone who can assist

examples.en: I offered to go for help because I knew where the staff room was.
examples.zh: 我知道员工休息室在哪，就主动说「去找人帮忙」。

examples.en: My friend told me she was going to go for help upstairs.
examples.zh: 朋友告诉我，她要到楼上「去找人帮忙」。

collocations: ask someone to go for help

words.enDefinition: to let an employee at the venue know what happened

examples.en: The organiser asked me to notify a member of staff at the entrance.
examples.zh: 组织者让我「通知一位入口处的工作人员」。

examples.en: I went downstairs to notify a member of staff after my friend fell.
examples.zh: 朋友摔倒后，我下楼「通知了一位工作人员」。

collocations: notify a member of staff immediately
ask someone to notify a member of staff
notify a member of staff at reception

words.enDefinition: a question identifying the person accompanying someone now

examples.en: The staff member asked, “Who is with them?” and looked toward the doorway.
examples.zh: 那名工作人员问「谁在陪着他们？」同时朝门口望去。

examples.en: “Who is with them?” the coach asked when I reached the office.
examples.zh: 我到办公室时，教练问「谁在陪着他们？」

words.enDefinition: to remain beside someone until another person or event arrives

examples.en: I'll wait with them while you go and get the duty officer.
examples.zh: 你去找值班安全员，我「陪他们等着」。

examples.en: The classmates offered to wait with them until the receptionist came back.
examples.zh: 同学们提出「陪他们等着」，直到接待员回来。

collocations: ask someone to wait with them
wait with them until staff arrive

words.enDefinition: to remain close to a particular person or place

examples.en: I offered to stay nearby in case the staff needed another witness.
examples.zh: 我主动说可以「留在附近」，万一工作人员需要另一位目击者。

examples.en: She asked her roommate to stay nearby while she spoke with the officer.
examples.zh: 她请室友「留在附近」，自己和安全员交谈。

collocations: stay nearby for a few minutes

words.enDefinition: to make more room by moving people or things aside

examples.en: The instructor asked the group to clear some space near the side door.
examples.zh: 老师请大家在侧门旁「腾出些空间」。

examples.en: We moved our bags to clear some space beside the room's entrance.
examples.zh: 我们把包挪开，在房间入口旁「腾出些空间」。

collocations: clear some space by the door
clear some space on the floor
ask people to clear some space

words.enDefinition: to step away so someone has more room or privacy

examples.en: The coach asked the gathering players to give them some space to speak privately.
examples.zh: 教练请围过来的队员「给他们留点空间」，好让他们单独谈谈。

examples.en: I stepped back to give them some space while they answered the officer.
examples.zh: 他们回答安全员的问题时，我往后退了退，「给他们留点空间」。

collocations: ask people to give them some space
step back to give them some space

words.enDefinition: to leave a passage free of obstructions so people can get through

examples.en: The staff asked us to keep the corridor clear outside the sports hall.
examples.zh: 工作人员请我们「保持体育馆外的走廊畅通」。

examples.en: The notice said to keep the corridor clear during the evening event.
examples.zh: 通知要求晚间活动期间「保持走廊畅通」。

collocations: keep the corridor clear of bags
ask everyone to keep the corridor clear
keep the corridor clear for staff

words.enDefinition: to assume responsibility for what happens from this point

examples.en: The duty officer thanked me and said, “I'll take it from here.”
examples.zh: 值班安全员向我道了谢，说「接下来我来处理」。

examples.en: I asked if the event organiser could take it from here while I called home.
examples.zh: 我问活动组织者能不能「接手处理接下来的事」，我好给家里打个电话。

collocations: can you take it from here
let someone take it from here

words.enDefinition: to pass responsibility for a person or situation to someone else

examples.en: I waited to hand over to the campus staff who had just arrived.
examples.zh: 我等着跟刚到场的「校园工作人员交接」。

examples.en: The event volunteer was ready to hand over to the duty officer.
examples.zh: 活动志愿者做好了和「值班安全员交接」的准备。

collocations: prepare to hand over to staff
hand over to the person on duty
wait to hand over to a colleague

words.enDefinition: to relay what you know to another person who needs it

examples.en: I asked the receptionist to pass on the details to the staff upstairs.
examples.zh: 我请接待员帮忙把「具体情况转告」楼上的工作人员。

examples.en: Could you pass on the details when the event organiser comes back?
examples.zh: 活动组织者回来时，你能「转告具体情况」吗？

collocations: pass on the details to staff
offer to pass on the details
pass on the details by phone

words.enDefinition: to tell someone the latest information about an ongoing situation

examples.en: I went back to give an update to the tutor who was still waiting.
examples.zh: 我回到还在等消息的导师那里，「说明最新情况」。

examples.en: The receptionist asked me to give an update when the first aider arrived.
examples.zh: 接待员让我在急救员到场后「说一下最新情况」。

collocations: give an update on the situation
give an update to the coordinator

words.enDefinition: to ask someone to contact your roommate by phone

examples.en: Could you call my roommate and tell her I'm with the event staff?
examples.zh: 你能「打给我室友」，告诉她我和活动工作人员在一起吗？

examples.en: I asked the receptionist to call my roommate because my phone was upstairs.
examples.zh: 我手机落在楼上了，就请接待员「打给我室友」。

collocations: ask someone to call my roommate

words.enDefinition: a question asking permission to sit in a particular place

examples.en: “Can I sit here?” I asked when the staff member came over.
examples.zh: 工作人员走过来时，我问「我能坐这儿吗？」

examples.en: She pointed to the chair by the door and asked, “Can I sit here?”
examples.zh: 她指着门边的椅子问「我能坐这儿吗？」

collocations: “Can I sit here for a minute?”
“Can I sit here while I wait?”

words.enDefinition: a display of symbols, pictures or words for expressing messages

examples.en: She pointed to a word on her communication board rather than saying it aloud.
examples.zh: 她没有把那个词说出来，而是指向了「沟通板」上的相应词语。

examples.en: The volunteer asked whether the communication board was within the student's reach.
examples.zh: 志愿者问，那位学生能不能够到自己的「沟通板」。

collocations: point to a symbol on a communication board

words.enDefinition: an app that speaks typed or displayed words aloud

examples.en: My roommate used a text-to-speech app to tell the supervisor what she needed.
examples.zh: 室友用「文字转语音应用」告诉主管她需要什么。

examples.en: I asked whether a text-to-speech app would be easier for him to use.
examples.zh: 我问他用「文字转语音应用」会不会更方便。

words.enDefinition: a small device that helps a person hear sounds

examples.en: The student said his hearing aid had fallen out near the bench.
examples.zh: 那位学生说，他的「助听器」掉在长凳附近了。

examples.en: I found a hearing aid case beside the bag she had left behind.
examples.zh: 我在她留下的包旁边发现了一个「助听器」盒。

words.enDefinition: the way someone wants to exchange information with others

examples.en: The staff member asked about my preferred communication method before giving me an update.
examples.zh: 工作人员在告诉我最新情况前，先问了我的「首选沟通方式」。

examples.en: I mentioned that typing was my preferred communication method in this noisy room.
examples.zh: 我提到，在这个嘈杂的房间里，打字是我的「首选沟通方式」。

collocations: ask about someone's preferred communication method

words.enDefinition: to take turns speaking so voices do not overlap

examples.en: Could you speak one at a time so I can follow what's happening?
examples.zh: 你们能「一个一个说」吗？这样我才能听清现在的情况。

examples.en: The teacher asked everyone to speak one at a time while she took notes.
examples.zh: 老师请大家「一个一个说」，她来做记录。

collocations: ask people to speak one at a time
take turns and speak one at a time
speak one at a time during the discussion

words.expression: give me a moment to answer
words.lemma: give me a moment to answer
words.enDefinition: to allow the speaker a little time before they reply
acceptedEnVariants: give me a moment to answer

examples.en: Could you give me a moment to answer before asking the next question?
examples.zh: 问下一个问题之前，能「让我想一下再回答」吗？

examples.en: I asked her to give me a moment to answer while I found my phone.
examples.zh: 我在找手机，请她「给我一点时间再回答」。

collocations: please give me a moment to answer
can you give me a moment to answer
ask someone to give me a moment to answer

words.zhGloss: 可以把刚才说的写下来吗
words.enDefinition: a request to record spoken information in writing
acceptedZhAnswers: 可以把刚才说的写下来吗

examples.en: Could you write that down so I can read it at my own pace?
examples.zh: 「可以把刚才说的写下来吗？」我想按自己的速度看。

examples.en: “Could you write that down?” I asked when the announcement drowned out her voice.
examples.zh: 广播盖过了她的声音，我问「可以把刚才说的写下来吗？」

collocations: “Could you write that down for me?”
“Could you write that down on this page?”

words.zhGloss: 能去安静一点的地方说吗
words.enDefinition: a request to move a conversation somewhere with less noise
acceptedZhAnswers: 能去安静一点的地方说吗

examples.en: “Can we talk somewhere quieter?” I asked as the crowd grew louder.
examples.zh: 人群越来越吵，我问「能去安静一点的地方说吗？」

examples.en: She looked towards the side room and asked, “Can we talk somewhere quieter?”
examples.zh: 她朝旁边那间屋看了一眼，问「能去安静一点的地方说吗？」

collocations: “Can we talk somewhere quieter for a minute?”
“Can we talk somewhere quieter than this?”

words.expression: I can't see without my glasses
words.lemma: i can't see without my glasses
words.enDefinition: a statement explaining that you need your glasses to see
acceptedEnVariants: I can't see without my glasses

examples.en: I can't see without my glasses, and I think they're under the chair.
examples.zh: 「不戴眼镜我看不清」，我想眼镜在椅子底下。

examples.en: “I can't see without my glasses,” he explained when she held up the form.
examples.zh: 她举起表格时，他解释道「不戴眼镜我看不清」。

collocations: say “I can't see without my glasses”
“I can't see without my glasses on”
“I can't see without my glasses, so could you read it aloud?”

words.enDefinition: a request to express one's own account or preferences directly

examples.en: “Can I speak for myself?” she asked before her friend answered again.
examples.zh: 朋友又要替她回答时，她问「我可以自己说吗？」

examples.en: I wanted to explain what I needed, so I asked, “Can I speak for myself?”
examples.zh: 我想亲口说自己需要什么，于是问「我可以自己说吗？」

collocations: “Can I speak for myself this time?”
“Can I speak for myself for a moment?”

words.expression: I'd like them to stay with me
words.lemma: i'd like them to stay with me
words.zhGloss: 我想让他们留下来陪我
words.enDefinition: a request for another person to remain present for support
acceptedZhAnswers: 我想让他们留下来陪我
acceptedEnVariants: I'd like them to stay with me

examples.en: “I'd like them to stay with me,” she said, pointing to her roommate.
examples.zh: 她指了指室友，说「我想让她留下来陪我」。

examples.en: The student told the staff member, “I'd like them to stay with me.”
examples.zh: 那位学生对工作人员说「我想让他们留下来陪我」。

collocations: say “I'd like them to stay with me”
“I'd like them to stay with me while we talk”
“I'd like them to stay with me a little longer”

words.enDefinition: to seek permission before making physical contact

examples.en: I asked the volunteer to ask before touching me or my wheelchair.
examples.zh: 我请志愿者在「碰我或我的轮椅前先问一声」。

examples.en: The accessibility guide asked staff to ask before touching a visitor's mobility equipment.
examples.zh: 无障碍指南要求工作人员「碰访客的助行设备前先问一声」。

words.enDefinition: to say written words so another person can hear them

examples.en: The form was hard to read, so I asked her to read it aloud.
examples.zh: 表格看不清楚，我便请她「读出来」。

examples.en: Could you read it aloud while I look for my glasses in the bag?
examples.zh: 我在包里找眼镜，你能「把它读出来」吗？

collocations: ask someone to read it aloud

words.enDefinition: the staff member currently responsible for responding to calls or incidents

examples.en: The duty officer at the residence desk asked who had seen the incident.
examples.zh: 宿舍前台的「值班负责人」问，谁看到了事情经过。

examples.en: The event steward left my name with the duty officer at the gate.
examples.zh: 活动引导员把我的姓名留给了门口的「值班负责人」。

collocations: hand over to the duty officer

words.enDefinition: remaining on the floor after sitting down or falling

examples.en: I told the staff member she was still on the floor by the bench.
examples.zh: 我告诉工作人员，她「还在长凳旁的地上」。

examples.en: He was still on the floor when his teammate came back with the coach.
examples.zh: 队友带着教练回来时，他「还在地上」。

collocations: find someone still on the floor
someone is still on the floor
still on the floor by the bench

words.expression: could you say that again slowly
words.lemma: could you say that again slowly
words.enDefinition: a request for someone to repeat their words at a slower pace
acceptedEnVariants: could you say that again slowly

examples.en: “Could you say that again slowly?” I asked as the room grew louder.
examples.zh: 屋里越来越吵，我问「能慢一点再说一遍吗？」

examples.en: The student said, “Could you say that again slowly?” and turned toward the speaker.
examples.zh: 那名学生转向说话的人，问「能慢一点再说一遍吗？」

collocations: ask “Could you say that again slowly?”
“Could you say that again slowly, please?”
“Could you say that again slowly so I can write it down?”
